note: Literature check of 15 Nov 2026 for the Combinatorics Wiki's table of the largest known Cayley graphs (page saved 15 Nov 2026 12:13 UTC). The table is behind: F. Comellas's tables of the largest known (degree, diameter)-graphs (web.mat.upc.edu/francesc.comellas/delta-d/desc_g/desc_g2.html to desc_g10.html, read 15 Nov 2026 18:47 UTC, ten seconds between requests; the site serves no robots.txt) describe many Cayley graphs found in 2024-2026 that are larger than the wiki's entries, and M. Macaj (New computational results for the degree/diameter problem for 4-valent Cayley graphs, CEUR-WS Vol-4323, paper 33, 2026) settles two cells and raises two. The best known value of a cell is the largest of the wiki's value, the largest graph that Comellas's pages describe as a Cayley graph for that degree and diameter (tools/combwiki_cayley_cells.py reads the pages: an entry or former result counts when its own description says it is a Cayley graph, and not when it says bi-Cayley, not Cayley, a Cayley controller graph, the split Cayley hexagon or 'Cayley ? False'; where the description names the group Z_m (x) Z_n, m n must equal the order) and the papers below.
